issues.failure_explanation: For a flow of v with Phi_* nu, change of variables and Liouville's formula give log f_{Phi_* nu}(y) = log f_nu(Phi^{-1}(y)) - int_0^1 div v_t(Phi_t(Phi^{-1}(y))) dt. The displayed formula has the opposite sign and evaluates the divergence along Phi_t(y) instead of along the backward trajectory through y. Counterexample: v(x)=lambda x in 1D. Then Phi(x)=e^lambda x and log f_{Phi_* nu}(y) = log f_nu(e^{-lambda} y) - lambda, while the display gives +lambda. The same passage says samples from Phi_* nu are obtained as x=Phi^{-1}(z), which is also the wrong direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display by log f_nu(Phi^{-1}(y)) - int_0^1 div v_t(Phi_t(Phi^{-1}(y))) dt, and correct the sampling sentence to x=Phi(z).
issues.overall_effect: The stated likelihood representation is false as written. Later proofs use the change-of-variables formula directly, so no theorem is affected.
issues.title: Liouville log-density formula has wrong sign and wrong evaluation point
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a motivating formula; nothing downstream depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Inserting into the determinant sensitivity bound~\cite[Cor.~2.14]{ipsen2008} yields

issues.failure_explanation: The proofs bound |log|det A| - log|det B|| for A=D[Phi^theta]^{-1}(x), B=D[Phi^mu]^{-1}(x) (or theta') by sum_k C(d,k) 2^k ||A-B||^k. This contains no dependence on ||A^{-1}|| or a lower bound on |det|, so it cannot hold for general matrices. Counterexample: A=eps I, B=2 eps I gives a log-difference of d log 2 while the right side tends to 0 as eps tends to 0. A correct log-det bound is relative and needs ||A^{-1}|| = ||D Phi|| controlled. Only upper bounds on ||D[Phi]^{-1}|| (Gronwall) are established, and the step passing from a determinant difference to a log difference is not justified. The same step is used in three proofs.

failure_location.quote: Thus, the determinant sensitivity estimate from~\cite[Cor.~2.14]{ipsen2008} yields

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a correct log-det perturbation estimate. Bound ||D Phi|| (or the Jacobian determinant from below) by Gronwall/Liouville, or bound the log-determinant difference directly through the divergence integral. Then re-derive the constants in the model-error theorem, the sub-Gaussian lemma and the concentration theorem; their exponential form should survive.
issues.overall_effect: The KL model-error bound (kl_target_approx_thm), the Lipschitz and sub-Gaussian constant bar L, the bounded-difference constant D, and the final PAC theorem all rest on an unproven inequality.
issues.title: Log-determinant perturbation bound used without lower bounds on the determinants
issues.why_classification: It needs a contained new estimate and changed constants, but the architecture of the argument and the form of the results survive.

issues.failure_explanation: eps^gen is the supremum of |Z_theta,n|, but it is set equal to E[sup Z_theta,n]. Dudley's bound controls the signed supremum, and passing to absolute values costs an extra argument and a constant factor, so the constant 48 is not justified. The integral is written over (0,infinity) with the volumetric bound (1+2 sqrt q/eps)^q, for which it diverges. The proof silently truncates at eps = sqrt q, which is legitimate only for the true covering number.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply Dudley to both Z and -Z, or to sup |Z_theta - Z_theta0| plus |Z_theta0|, truncate the entropy integral at the diameter, and adjust the numerical constant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated constant 48 L W^2 bar L/sqrt n in the expected generalization bound, and its reuse in the concentration theorem and the main proof, is not established as written. Only the order of the bound is unaffected.
issues.title: Dudley step treats the supremum of |Z| as the supremum of Z and uses an unbounded entropy integral
issues.why_classification: Only the numerical constant changes; the rate and the structure of the argument are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The decomposition derived earlier (and correct by the ERM argument) has coefficient 2 on eps^gen. The proof cites it as having coefficient 1. The subsequent chain of thresholds (eps^2/(16||qoi||^2), eps^2/(32||qoi||^2), 4096) was computed with the wrong decomposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the factor 2 through: require eps^gen > eps^2/(32||qoi||^2) and adjust the thresholds and the constant 4096 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants in the probability bound and in n(epsilon,delta) are not those that follow from the stated decomposition.
issues.title: Main proof drops the factor 2 on the generalization error in the risk decomposition
issues.why_classification: A constants-only fix with no change to the argument or the conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which tends to zero as $n \to \infty$, since $\beta < \frac{1}{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Only the upper bound bar L <= c n^beta is available, so the stated assumption would give 48 L W^2 bar L/sqrt n <= 48 bar L^2/sqrt n <= c n^{2 beta - 1/2}. That tends to 0 only for beta < 1/4, not for the claimed range beta in (0,1/2). The conclusion n_2(epsilon) exists is true, but only because L_n W_n^2 grows polylogarithmically (W_n = floor(log log n)). That fact is not what the text invokes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the assumption by the bound L_n W_n^2 = O((log log n)^3) and combine it with bar L/sqrt n <= c n^{beta-1/2}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the inference supporting the full range beta < 1/2 in the main theorem is invalid.
issues.title: Unjustified assumption L_n W_n^2 <= bar L used to conclude the vanishing of the expected generalization bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, for any architecture parameters $L_n, W_n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, it is possible to choose a threshold $m(n)$ for the number of quadrature points
for all sample sizes $n,m \geq n(\varepsilon,\delta), m(\varepsilon,\delta)$

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd) involves the factor exp(sqrt d sqrt q Lip_1^Theta(L_n,W_n,d)). Here q, L_n and W_n grow with n, and Lip_1 >= Lip_0 = L(2W)^{...}(d+1)^{...} tends to infinity. Hence the m needed to reach epsilon/2 depends on n and is unbounded in n. The proof fixes m at the value for n = n(epsilon,delta) and asserts the bound for all larger n. That is false for the constant being used. The theorem's claim of n-independent thresholds (PAC in the sense of defn:pac_learnability) is therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: and a threshold $m(\varepsilon, \delta) := m(n(\varepsilon, \delta))$ on the number of quadrature points such that \eqref{eq:main_thm_sg_error_bd} holds, for all $n \geq n(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and all $m \geq m(\varepsilon,\delta)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with the quadrature threshold depending on n (m >= m(n,epsilon) with an explicit, very fast growth), or establish an n-independent bound on ||Phi^{theta_n}||_{C^1} for the learned maps. Adjust the PAC definition and abstract accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: What the proof supports is a coupled statement (m >= m(n) growing very fast with n), not the claimed independent thresholds n(epsilon,delta), m(epsilon,delta). The PAC claim of the main theorem and the abstract are overstated.
issues.title: Quadrature threshold m(epsilon,delta) treated as independent of n although the quadrature constant grows with the architecture
issues.why_classification: The result survives as a coupled-limit consistency statement with a contained restatement and no new global architecture, but the advertised independence of the thresholds is lost.
